name: Belshazzar
title: The Last King of Babylon
summary: Belshazzar was the last king of the Neo-Babylonian Empire and ruled as co-regent under his father Nabonidus. He is best known for the grand feast where a hand wrote on the wall, prophesying the fall of the kingdom. That same night, he was killed when the Persians conquered Babylon.

keyEvents.title: The Great Feast
keyEvents.description: Belshazzar held a great feast for a thousand of his nobles and drank wine with them, and he commanded that the gold and silver vessels from the temple in Jerusalem be brought.

keyEvents.title: The Writing on the Wall
keyEvents.description: During the feast, fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the wall. The king was terrified, and his face grew pale.

keyEvents.title: Daniel Is Summoned
keyEvents.description: After the wise men failed to interpret the writing, Daniel was brought in at the queen's advice to explain the message on the wall.

keyEvents.title: Daniel's Rebuke
keyEvents.description: Daniel reminded Belshazzar of his ancestor Nebuchadnezzar's pride and punishment, and accused him of not humbling himself but dishonoring God by using the temple vessels.

keyEvents.title: The Judgment Proclaimed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPARSIN
keyEvents.description: Daniel interpreted the writing as God's judgment on Belshazzar: his days were numbered, he had been weighed and found wanting, and the kingdom would be divided between the Medes and Persians.

keyEvents.title: Belshazzar's Death and the Fall of Babylon
keyEvents.description: That same night Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was killed, and Darius the Mede took over the kingdom.
